newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.S.-pledged Bosnian arms due to arrive on Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-pledged Bosnian arms due to arrive on Friday.

text.p: The main shipment of a $100 million arms package for Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation is due to arrive in the Adriatic port of Ploce on Friday, a U.S. official said.
Joseph Allred, spokesman for the American "train and equip" programme, said the shipment will include 45 tanks, 79 armoured personnel carriers, 15 helicopters, ammunition and communication equipment.

The programme, combining military hardware and instruction for federation army troops, was devised to ensure a parity of forces in the region and help the federation army counter any future threat from its Serb foes.
"The train and equip programme, together with the arms reduction programme of the international community, should achieve a balance in Bosnia," Allred said on Wednesday.
European powers have criticised Washington's "train and equip" programme, saying it undermined diplomatic goals to promote reconciliation and arms control in Bosnia.
Some Bosnian Moslem officials have also privately criticised the American aid package, saying it provided primarily symbolic assistance.

The Moslem-led Bosnian army was outgunned by Serb forces during the 43-month war and had to rely on Islamic countries such as Iran for arms shipments, which violated an international arms embargo on former Yugoslavia.
The U.S. in August sent a symbolic shipment of 1,000 M-16 rifles with ammunition but with the delivery of the remaining equipment the $100 million donation will be completed, Allred said.
The instruction of Bosnian soldiers began in October, when a team of 170 retired U.S. officers, hired by the federation authorities, launched a training programme in an officers school near Sarajevo.
The retired officers, from the private firm MPRI based in Alexandria, Virginia, also started field training of two Bosnian army brigades.

Allred said the U.S.-donated weapons will be transported from Ploce port to federation storage sites, but it was yet to be decided whether the equipment would be delivered by road or via the newly reconstructed railway to Bosnia.
